+Use `*` as the rule name to turn off every rule of a plugin. In the same table, a setting for a single rule overrides the wildcard, in either order.
+- A wildcard can only be `"off"`. To turn rules on, name them or use [`lint.categories`](#lint-categories).
+- [`lint.overrides`](#lint-overrides) and flags apply after `[lint.rules]`. A wildcard there also turns off a rule that `[lint.rules]` sets by name.
+- `"react/*"` leaves `react/jsx-uses-react` on. That rule reports nothing. It keeps `no-unused-vars` quiet about `React`.

+- A wildcard works with Bun's own lint config. If the working directory has an ESLint or oxlint config, `bun lint` rejects the wildcard. Files under a config file in a nested directory follow that file, and the wildcard doesn't apply to them.

Some ESLint rules have a typescript-eslint version, such as `no-unused-vars` and `@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars`. Setting either name sets both. The ESLint rule runs on JavaScript files and the typescript-eslint rule on TypeScript files, so a problem is never reported twice. If you set both names, each one applies to its own kind of file.

+A wildcard is about one plugin, so it turns such a rule off in one language. `"@typescript-eslint/*" = "off"` turns `no-unused-vars` off in TypeScript files and leaves it on in JavaScript files. `"eslint/*" = "off"` does the opposite.

A few typescript-eslint versions need type information, such as `@typescript-eslint/require-await`. Setting that name type checks your TypeScript files, like any other [type-aware rule](/lint#type-aware-rules). Setting only `require-await` doesn't start a type check. It uses the typescript-eslint version if the run has types anyway, and the ESLint rule otherwise.

+A category sets the rules of every built-in plugin. The plugins for a framework or a test runner are the exception. A category sets their rules only if `package.json` lists the package in `dependencies`, `devDependencies`, or `peerDependencies`.

+For each file, Bun reads the closest `package.json` that lists dependencies. Monorepos often list the test runner only in the root `package.json`. If the closest `package.json` lists neither `jest` nor `vitest`, Bun also looks in the ones above it, up to the root of the Git repository.
+`[lint.rules]` doesn't depend on `package.json`. To turn off a plugin that a category turns on, set `"unicorn/*" = "off"`. To use a plugin without its package, set `"jsx-a11y/*" = "warn"`.
